actions.justification: First step in any clinical encounter - obtain comprehensive history including chief complaint, HF history, medications, functional status, and symptoms to guide diagnosis and management.
Perform thorough physical examination to assess for signs of heart failure (JVD, peripheral edema, S3 gallop, crackles) and hemodynamic status.
Mandatory diagnostic: ECG is essential to identify arrhythmias, ischemia, conduction abnormalities, or LVH that may be contributing to or causing heart failure presentation.
Mandatory lab to assess renal function, electrolytes, and glucose — critical for heart failure evaluation and guiding treatment.
Mandatory biomarker to confirm heart failure diagnosis and assess severity/prognosis per HF guidelines.
Mandatory lab to evaluate for anemia (a common HF exacerbating factor) and identify infection or other hematologic abnormalities.

Mandatory action - chest X-ray is essential to evaluate for pulmonary congestion, pleural effusions, and cardiomegaly in the workup of suspected heart failure. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.
Mandatory action - TSH is required to rule out thyroid dysfunction as a reversible cause of heart failure or exacerbating factor. Must be completed within 60-minute deadline.
Assessing hemodynamic profile (wet/dry, warm/cold) will guide targeted therapy selection and help determine if diuretics, vasodilators, or advanced therapies are needed.

Echocardiographic assessment of LVEF is a critical next step in heart failure workup to guide therapy decisions (HFrEF vs HFpEF) and determine appropriateness of GDMT including beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, and device therapy.
Once LVEF is known, ICD indication assessment is warranted per guideline recommendations for patients with reduced EF to prevent sudden cardiac death.
CRT indication should be evaluated in heart failure patients with reduced LVEF, particularly if QRS prolongation or LBBB pattern was noted on ECG, as this can reduce morbidity and mortality.

NYHA functional classification is essential to guide heart failure management, determine appropriate therapies, and assess prognosis. This has not yet been completed and is a foundational step in HF evaluation.
Assessment of structural abnormalities (e.g., via echocardiographic findings) is needed to guide therapy decisions including device therapy and advanced treatment options in heart failure.
With LVEF assessment completed, evaluating candidacy for advanced therapies (LVAD, transplant) is appropriate as part of comprehensive HF workup, particularly if EF is reduced.
With a stable heart failure patient who has completed initial workup, assessing whether GDMT is optimized and duration is appropriate is a key next step in management per heart failure guidelines.
Patient HR is 80 bpm; if this is a heart failure with reduced EF patient in sinus rhythm with HR ≥70 on maximally tolerated beta-blocker, ivabradine may be indicated per ACC/AHA HF guidelines.
Cardiac rehabilitation is recommended for stable heart failure patients to improve functional capacity and quality of life per guideline recommendations.
Confirm the patient is on optimal guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, which is the foundation of management after completing the initial workup.
ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan) are Class I recommended therapy for HFrEF to reduce mortality and morbidity. Patient's BP 120/80 is acceptable for initiation/continuation.

Beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol) are Class I recommended therapy for HFrEF. HR of 80 is within acceptable range and patient is hemodynamically stable for initiation/continuation.

MRA (e.g., spironolactone/eplerenone) is a key component of GDMT for HFrEF when not already optimized. Patient is hemodynamically stable with adequate BP, making addition of MRA appropriate per heart failure guidelines to reduce mortality and hospitalizations.
Assess and address volume status with diuretic therapy if signs of congestion are present. This is standard heart failure management to relieve symptoms and optimize fluid balance.

Given that advanced therapy candidacy was already assessed, proceeding with comprehensive transplant workup is the next logical step if the patient meets criteria for advanced heart failure therapies.
